# Five releases in a day: Blygger Studio 0.42 to 0.46

Blygger Studio shipped five releases on October 12. Most of what changed is visible on the public side of a blyg: how its home page reads, how a reader finds their way around it, and what the owner can put where. Each release has its own announcement, linked under each section; this is the tour.



## A home page that keeps time two ways

0.42.0 added the **pace-layered home page**. Items sink as new ones arrive and climb one place with each new version, and pins slow the sinking, so what keeps mattering stays near the top while what is new still arrives. It reads only what any subscriber can see (changelogs, pins, quotes), so other clients can compute the same order. It is the default for fresh installs; a blyg that has already published keeps newest first until its owner chooses. The same release added a **setup walk-through** that shows every setting beside its default.


Release notes: [[1q4zp1efmn4ffbaa5xshyf8vsd]]


## A static front page

0.43.0 lets a blyg greet readers with **a thread of its owner's choosing** at its root, the way a WordPress site can use a static front page. The latest items move to `/posts/` (the address is a setting), and every public page links there. The thread is still an ordinary thread: edited like any other and still in the feed, the archive and the index, so nothing changes for other blygs reading it. The release also removed an intermittent `CancelledError` banner while editing, a fix contributed by Kyle Mathews.


Release notes: [[2qnspef760dpa71b61vrg5jb0a]]


## A main menu, and a masthead menu

0.44.0 added a **menu on every public page**: threads the owner picks (an About page, a Now page), public collections, the owner's own links, and a line of standard links to the blogroll's OPML file, blygger.org and blygger.com. 0.45.0 made it a proper **side menu**, one link per line in a narrow column with the blyg's name set over the content, and on a phone a **Menu** button under the name instead of a list at the foot of the page. Since 0.46.0 it sits on the left by default.


Release notes: [[2zmmjmw81259fpqakcyf6qqxr6]], [[1nbe3sakyg9bkz99mj0r4e77hs]]


## Your own posts in hoppers

Hoppers used to hold only what you read. Since 0.45.0 an owner can put **their own posts in a hopper** beside other people's, from a post's menu, and a public hopper's page shows them as the home page would. A hopper can now be a reading list, a portfolio, or both.


Release notes: [[1nbe3sakyg9bkz99mj0r4e77hs]]


## Writing without the buttons going grey

Autosave used to disable *publish* and *save draft* every time the writer paused, until the save came back. Since 0.45.0 it saves quietly, and a publish clicked meanwhile waits for the save and publishes the newest text.


Release notes: [[1nbe3sakyg9bkz99mj0r4e77hs]]


## Settings on one page

0.46.0 reorganizes **Settings** into one page with a sidebar: General, Feed, Appearance, Links, AI, Network. Under Links, the two menus are named for where they appear: the *masthead menu* under the author's name and the *main menu* beside the content. Under AI, each function's model sits beside its own instructions, so `[TK]` generation, change notes and the smart feed each read as one unit. Choosing a front page or a menu thread is now a search rather than a long list.


Release notes: [[3xtkkjdjtscjcw250gnv75z54g]]


## Next on the roadmap

Five items joined the [roadmap](https://blygger.org/roadmap/) along the way: the owner API moving under the blyg's own address, so a blyg can share a domain with other software (asked for by Surya Kasturi); `[[text | id]]` links with chosen link text; links written by `[TK]` generation that currently publish as raw brackets; the blogroll listed entry by entry in the main menu; and a pace-layered order for the reading view.
